22.0.s.en: (1) Conditions for the priests' eating of the sacrifice

22.0.1.en: The holy things of the children of Israel: the foods that the priests eat from the offerings and sacrifices of the children of Israel to God. God asked Moses to teach Aaron and his sons the priests to respect the holy things of God, eating them with fear and reverence and not like the rest of their foods, for in this eating of theirs they perform a divine work, since they proclaim God's acceptance The Book of Exodus of the sacrifices and offerings of the people, and they feel that God is the Giver of this food and its Blesser, so they eat it with joy and humility. For their eating these holy things with greed or with evil desire, as if it were ordinary food, is a defiling and a despising of God.

22.1.0.en: To confirm the reverence due from the priests and their households for the Lord's portion of the foods which they eat, He warns them against eating of it if any of them has an uncleanness for any of the reasons mentioned previously in this book. Whoever makes light of it and eats of these foods while his uncleanness is upon him is cut off from the priesthood and deprived of service before God, that is, he is removed far from God, because he has defiled His holy things.

22.2.0.en: He gives examples of cases of uncleanness that are barred from eating the holy things of God, which are:

22.2.1.en: 1- The priest who is afflicted with leprosy (ch. 13, 14).

22.2.2.en: 2- The priest who is afflicted with a discharge (ch. 15:1-15).

22.2.3.en: 3- The priest who touches a dead person or something belonging to him (ch. 21).

22.2.4.en: 4- A priest who has had marital relations with his wife (ch. 15:16-18).

22.2.5.en: 5- A priest who has touched an unclean creeping animal, or anything touched by the carcass of that unclean animal (ch. 11:24-44).

22.2.6.en: 6- A priest who has touched an unclean person, with any kind of uncleanness.

22.3.0.en: If any priest is made unclean by any of the preceding uncleannesses or by any other kind of uncleanness, he remains unclean until evening, then he washes his whole body, and after that he is permitted to eat of the holy things of God, which are his food.

22.4.0.en: All the people were forbidden to eat animals that had died or been torn by beasts, because their blood is in them (ch. 17:15, 16); how much more is the priest not permitted to eat of them, lest he defile himself.

22.5.0.en: My ordinance: My worship and My statutes.

22.5.1.en: God warns His priests to be exacting in applying His Law in their worship of Him; as for whoever makes light of it, he exposes himself to death as the punishment for despising the Law of God.

22.6.0.en: The portion of the priests from the sacrifices and offerings of God is eaten by him and his seed, that is, his wife and his children only, and it is not permitted for any of the following to eat of it:

22.6.1.en: 1- Strangers, that is, Jews who are not of the seed of the priests (Num 1:15).

22.6.2.en: 2- Sojourners, that is, guests, whether they are Jews or non-Jews.

22.6.3.en: 3- Hired servants, that is, those who work for the priests, whether temporary slaves or day laborers, Jews or non-Jews.

22.6.4.en: In sum, these holy foods (such as his portion of the peace offering) are enjoyed only by the priest and his household, as a divine grace with which God favors the priest and his household, and they signify the blessing of God given to the priests and servants.

22.6.5.en: If you serve God and labor for His sake, know that He is rich and is not indebted to anyone, but He will bless you with many blessings by which you are distinguished from others, not only material blessings but rather spiritual blessings that advance you on the road to the Kingdom; so seize every opportunity to offer Him your love.

22.7.0.en: Those permitted to eat of the holy things of God, other than the priest's household, are:

22.7.1.en: 1- The slaves whom the priest bought and circumcised, so that they became Jews residing permanently with the priest.

22.7.2.en: 2- Slaves born to male and female slaves who reside permanently in the priest's house; these are circumcised and permitted to eat.

22.8.0.en: The priest's daughter eats of the holy things of God, and if she marries a priest she will also eat of them, but if she marries a stranger, that is, a Jew who is not of the priests, she is under his care and belongs to him, and so she is deprived of the food of her father's house, which is the holy things of God.

22.9.0.en: It is also permitted to eat of the holy things for the following:

22.9.1.en: 1- The priest's daughter who married a stranger and then he divorced her, so she returned to her father's house.

22.9.2.en: 2- The widow whose stranger husband died and who bore no children by him, so she returned to her father's house. The Book of Exodus But the widow who bore children, whether she returned to her father's house or did not return, does not eat of the holy things, neither she nor her children, because her husband's family are responsible to provide for her.

22.9.3.en: 3- If the widow's children die, she returns to her father's house and is permitted to eat of the holy things.

22.10.0.en: If any Jewish person who is not of the seed of the priests eats of the holy things of God by oversight, that is, unintentionally, he has sinned, and he is to do the following:

22.10.1.en: 1- He offers a trespass offering, a ram for God.

22.10.2.en: 2- He gives food like what he ate and adds a fifth to it, as compensation and an apology for his error.

22.11.0.en: If some of the people sin and eat by oversight of the holy things of God that are set apart for the priests, or if the priests sin and eat of these holy things while they are unclean, then they:

22.11.1.en: 1- Profane the name of God and do not respect it.

22.11.2.en: 2- Defile the whole people, because they are individuals of it.

22.11.3.en: This makes a person careful in his worship and conduct, because his sin offends God and his whole family and community, and even encourages others to it, so that he spreads sin among people.

22.12.s.en: (2) Conditions for the vow and the freewill sacrifice

22.12.0.en: Their freewill offerings: the voluntary offerings other than those the Law prescribes, which are considered an offering of love to God in thanks for His kindnesses.

22.12.1.en: The conditions of the sacrifice that the Law prescribed were explained in the first chapters of this book, and the children of Israel used to offer additional offerings, such as vows, which are tied to a particular request from God, or freewill offerings, which are offerings of love to Him. God also requires that these be:

22.12.2.en: 1- From the herd, the sheep or the goats, which are the clean animals that the Law prescribed.

22.12.3.en: 2- A male, which signifies strength, so that the best is offered to God.

22.12.4.en: 3- Perfect: that is, without blemish, as a type of Christ, who is without sin and offered Himself as a sacrifice for us on the Cross.

22.13.0.en: The vow or freewill sacrifice was offered as a peace offering with these preceding conditions, out of love for God and to obtain His pleasure and blessing; but if anyone makes light of these conditions, this is considered making light of God and brings His anger upon him.

22.13.1.en: Having pustules: one who has pustules, that is, boils.

22.13.2.en: Spotted: one who has black dots, that is, freckles.

22.13.3.en: God forbids the offering of a sacrifice that has any blemish, and He specifies these blemishes, which are:

22.13.5.en: 2- Broken: having any part of its legs or bones broken.

22.13.6.en: 3- One that has a wound, new or old, which left a clear mark.

22.13.7.en: 4- Having pustules, because pustules mar its appearance.

22.13.8.en: 5- Scabbed: one that has been afflicted with scab disease.

22.13.9.en: 6- Spotted: that is, one whose skin has many patches that mar its appearance.

22.13.10.en: So no sacrifice with these blemishes is to be brought near on the altar of God.

22.14.0.en: Having anything superfluous: excessive length in one of the bones, or extra fingers.

22.14.1.en: The Book of Exodus Lacking in his parts: excessive smallness of the body.

22.14.2.en: It is not permitted to offer one with anything superfluous or one that is lacking in its parts in these sacrifices which the Law prescribes or in vows, but it is permitted in the case of the freewill offering, because it is a gift of love offered to God.

22.14.3.en: The peace offering and vows must be without blemish, because they signify Christ, but the freewill offering is a gift from man to God and may have small weaknesses, such as having anything superfluous or being lacking in its parts, because it signifies the weakness of man.

22.15.0.en: Bruised testicles: one whose testicle was struck so that it was damaged.

22.15.1.en: Crushed: its testicle was ruined by crushing.

22.15.2.en: Cut: its testicle was removed and cut off.

22.15.3.en: The Law forbids the offering of an animal whose testicle is damaged as a sacrifice to God, because it signifies the inability to beget, that is, the lack of spiritual fruit.

22.15.4.en: And God forbids them to castrate animals in any way, since some pagan worship commanded this.

22.16.0.en: From a stranger's hand: the animals bought from non-Jews.

22.16.1.en: God forbids them to buy animals that have blemishes, as was mentioned in the preceding verses, in order to offer them as sacrifices to God, so that they may obtain His pleasure with good and perfect sacrifices; for offering blemished sacrifices is making light of God and of His commands.

22.16.2.en: Give God the best of what you have, whether in time or in material gifts, so that your perfect love for Him may appear; then the house of God will be better than your own house, and you will care for the brethren of the Lord more than you care for yourself, or at least as you care for yourself.

22.17.0.en: In His commandments to Moses about offering sacrifices, God added that an animal is not to be offered before seven days from its birth, so that it will have enjoyed suckling from its mother during these days, which is important nourishment for the newborn, and so that its mother also may enjoy it and her motherhood be satisfied. To this extent the mercy of God appears in His Law, so that He may teach us kindness to animals, and all the more that we have compassion on our brothers and sisters, human beings. For this reason the Jews did not slaughter an animal to eat it before seven days from its birth.

22.17.1.en: May you feel the feelings of others around you, and find excuses for them in their errors and shortcomings, and be longsuffering toward them, and provide for their needs before they ask for them. And compassion is to be shown to all, even animals, because a merciful heart is merciful to the great and the small, the rich and the poor, man and animal.

22.18.0.en: To complete the feelings of mercy, the Law commands that the mother animal not be slaughtered with her young in one day; it is enough that the animal has lost its young or lost its mother, so it is not to be offered for slaughter on the same day, because it is affected by this loss. This is the divine mercy that God expects us to practice with one another, so that we are not harsh to a person and his child at the same time.

22.19.0.en: If a person offers a thank offering to God, that is, a peace offering, his purpose is to please God and obtain His blessing in his life; therefore he adheres to all the conditions previously mentioned in this book, which mean offering the best that he has, and that it be without blemish.

22.20.0.en: Here He stresses the importance of eating the peace offering on the same day, as came in (ch. 7:15), for it signifies the sacrifice of the Eucharist in the New Testament, which is eaten on the same day.

22.21.0.en: At the end of this chapter God asks them to be committed to carrying out His commandments in all their sacrifices, thereby declaring their fear of God and their love for Him, because any violation of His laws is contempt for and defiling of His name before themselves and before the peoples around them. And He reminds them of His love and care for them, for it is He who brought them out of Egypt with great power and preserved them in the wilderness, so they must live for Him and obey His commandments.

22.21.1.en: The feasts. First: the idea of the feast:

22.21.2.en: The word feast means a witness or an assembly, and the feasts are called the appointed seasons or religious celebrations, and what is meant by them is:

22.21.3.en: 1- Stopping work and devoting oneself to the worship of God.

22.21.4.en: 2- Remembering important spiritual events that bind people to the worship of God, to loving Him and to thanking Him for His kindnesses.

22.21.5.en: 3- The celebrations in the Old Testament signify Christ the Savior, His redemption and His blessing in our lives, in addition to many spiritual meanings which we will speak about in detail with each feast.

22.21.7.en: Because feasts are a spiritual idea necessary for the spiritual person, they continued in the New Testament also, but their occasions changed, since they came to center on the One signified, who is Christ, in addition to the feasts of the saints who lived their lives in faith in Christ.

22.21.8.en: Third: the feasts that the Law prescribed:

22.21.9.en: A- Weekly feasts: this is the Sabbath day (Ex 20:8-11), which the Jews keep as a feast and on which they worship God in their homes.

22.21.10.en: B- Monthly feasts: these are the beginnings of the months, called the new moons (Num 10:10, 28:11-15), on which they worship God and offer Him offerings, whether for the Temple or for the poor.

22.21.12.en: 1- The Feast of the Passover on the fourteenth of the first month (Ex 12).

22.21.13.en: 2- The Feast of Unleavened Bread, which follows the Feast of the Passover, for seven days (Ex 13).

22.21.14.en: 3- The Feast of the Firstfruits on the eighteenth day of the second month, a remembrance of the offering of the first ripe ear of grain.

22.21.15.en: 4- The Feast of Pentecost, called the Feast of Weeks, which falls in the sixth month (Ex 23:16).

22.21.16.en: 5- The Feast of Trumpets, which falls at the beginning of the seventh month (Lev 23:23, 24).

22.21.17.en: 6- The Day of Atonement, which falls on the tenth day of the seventh month (Lev 16).

22.21.18.en: 7- The Feast of Tabernacles, which falls on the fifteenth day of the seventh month (Lev 23:33-36). These months are the months of the religious year, whereas the first of the months of the civil year is the one corresponding to the seventh month of the religious year.

22.21.19.en: God commanded the carrying out of these feasts in two stages:

22.21.20.en: The first stage: this is immediately after the giving of the Law in the wilderness of Sinai, and it comprises the feasts of the Sabbath, the Passover, Unleavened Bread, Trumpets and the Atonement.

22.21.21.en: The second stage: this is after their entry into the land of Canaan, and it comprises the feasts of the Firstfruits, Pentecost and Tabernacles. And God commanded that all the males of the children of Israel appear at His house at three feasts (Ex 23:14-17), which are:

22.21.25.en: The males represented the whole family, and the woman also was permitted to attend these feasts, and if she did not attend, the male acted on her behalf.

22.21.26.en: D- Periodic feasts: that is, every several years, and they are:

22.21.28.en: 2- The year of Jubilee, that is, the fiftieth year (Lev 25:8-22). It is to be noted that God commanded these feasts to Moses and he wrote them in the books of Exodus, Leviticus and Numbers. Fourth: feasts added by the Jews: these are according to their historical occurrence, for important events passed in the life of the Jews and they added other feasts, which are:

22.21.29.en: 1- The Feast of the Dedication of Solomon's Temple after he built it, in the seventh month (1 Kgs 8:2).

22.21.30.en: 2- The remembrance of the restoration of the Temple at the hand of Zerubbabel in the twelfth month (Ezra 6:15).

22.21.31.en: 3- The Feast of the Renewal of the Temple, which Judas Maccabeus ordained, on the twenty-fifth of the ninth month, lasting eight days (1 Macc 4:59), (Jn 10:22).

22.21.32.en: 4- The remembrance of the dedication of the Temple of Herod the Great (Jn 2:20).

22.21.33.en: 5- The two feasts of Purim, on the fourteenth and fifteenth of the twelfth month, which Esther and Mordecai ordained in remembrance of God's deliverance of the children of Israel from the plot of Haman (Esth 9:29-32).

22.21.34.en: 6- The day which the Jews ordained in remembrance of Judith's victory over Holofernes, the commander of the armies of the Assyrians, and the deliverance of the children of Israel from him (Jdt 16:31).

22.21.35.en: 7- The feast of the appearance of the holy fire in the days of Nehemiah (2 Macc 1:18).

22.21.36.en: 8- The remembrance of their victory over Nicanor the commander at the hand of Judas Maccabeus on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month (1 Macc 7:48, 49).
